questions.title: Second highest salary
questions.prompt: Given employees(id, name, salary), write a query returning the second highest distinct salary, or NULL if it doesn't exist.
expectedConcepts: ORDER BY … OFFSET 1 LIMIT 1, or MAX with a subquery
Handling the empty case with a scalar subquery
questions.answerOutline: SELECT (SELECT DISTINCT salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC OFFSET 1 LIMIT 1) AS second_highest; or use DENSE_RANK() = 2.
commonMistakes: Returning no row instead of NULL
followUps: Performance on 100M rows: what index helps?
questions.rubricNotes: Reward tie handling and the window-function generalisation.

questions.title: Isolation levels
questions.prompt: Explain transaction isolation levels and the anomalies each one prevents.
expectedConcepts: Dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read
questions.answerOutline: Define each anomaly with an example, map the levels to the anomalies, note that PostgreSQL implementations differ from the textbook (e.g. no dirty reads), and explain that SERIALIZABLE requires retry logic.
followUps: How do you prevent double-booking a seat?
SELECT … FOR UPDATE vs optimistic locking
questions.rubricNotes: Concrete examples per anomaly separate a 4-5 from a 2-3.

questions.title: Designing indexes
questions.prompt: A query filters orders by customer_id and status, sorted by created_at DESC, with LIMIT 20. What index would you create and why?
expectedConcepts: Index supports both filter and sort, avoiding a sort step
questions.answerOutline: Equality columns first, then the sort column, so the database can walk the index in order and stop after 20 rows. Verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
commonMistakes: Putting the range or sort column first
followUps: What if status has only 3 values?
questions.rubricNotes: Look for reasoning about column order, not just 'add an index'.
